Project 2: rcapsule — Reproducibility Capsules & Multi-Target Containerization for R

Suggested GitHub Repo: rcapsule
GitHub One-Liner: Compile any R project, Quarto manuscript, or Shiny app into lean Docker/Apptainer containers with cryptographic reproducibility verification.
Topics: r-package, reproducibility, docker, apptainer, containers, quarto, shiny, open-science

Project Statement

Computational reproducibility in R routinely breaks down at the boundary between R and the operating system. While renv records R package versions, projects still fail to reproduce across machines and over time due to mismatched system libraries (gdal, cmake, libxml2), C++ toolchains, CmdStan, TMB, JAGS, LaTeX, or reticulate/Python environments—and deploying a Shiny application cleanly with background workers remains a steep DevOps hurdle for quantitative researchers. Commercial reproducibility platforms solve part of this problem, but lock researchers into proprietary hosted silos.

rcapsule is an open-source reproducibility capsule compiler and verifier for R. It inspects any R analysis repo, Quarto manuscript, or Shiny application, resolves the full stack of R packages, OS system dependencies, and scientific toolchains, and compiles lean, reproducible Dockerfiles, multi-service docker-compose.yml stacks, and HPC-ready Apptainer definitions. Beyond building containers, rcapsule provides a cryptographic verification auditor: it executes the project inside a clean container, hashes inputs, seeds, environment layers, and outputs into a signed capsule.json manifest, and certifies whether published tables, figures, and numerical artifacts reproduce bit-for-bit or within explicit Monte Carlo tolerances.

Why Existing R Tools Aren’t Enough

  • renv solves only the R library layer and breaks frequently on native/compiled scientific dependencies (cmdstanr, sf, rJava, RTMB, Python).
  • rix (Nix) offers strong reproducibility but has a steep learning curve and poor compatibility with standard university HPC environments and Docker-first cloud hosts.
  • containerit is largely stagnant and lacks modern Quarto, CmdStan, multi-service Shiny, Apptainer, and cryptographic verification auditing.

Core Architectural Pillars

  1. Full-Stack Project & Toolchain Scanner: Parses R scripts, Quarto/Rmd chunks, DESCRIPTION, renv.lock, and Shiny entry points to map R dependencies, OS system libraries (sysreqs), compiled engines (CmdStan, TMB/RTMB, JAGS, C++), Python/reticulate, and TinyTeX/LaTeX.
  2. Multi-Target Container Compiler: Emits optimized, layer-cached multi-stage Dockerfiles, production docker-compose.yml templates (e.g., Shiny + worker queue + reverse proxy/healthchecks), and HPC Apptainer .def recipes with pinned base digests.
  3. Cryptographic Provenance Manifest (capsule.json): Records git commit, OS/R/toolchain digests, RNG seeds, and SHA-256 hashes of every data input and generated output artifact.
  4. Reproducibility Verification Runner: Runs the full analysis in a clean container (with a deterministic local sandbox/mock runner when Docker isn’t installed), compares outputs against the recorded manifest with exact and numeric-tolerance comparators, and renders an HTML/Markdown verification certificate suitable for journal peer review.

v1 Definition of Done

  • Accurate static scanner handling standard R scripts, Quarto manuscripts, Shiny apps, and CmdStan/Rcpp dependencies.
  • Validated Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, and Apptainer .def emitters with lint/snapshot tests.
  • Working manifest generator and exact/tolerance diff verifier tested locally without requiring Docker (plus guarded live-Docker integration tests).
  • Comprehensive testthat suite, roxygen2 docs, vignettes, and clean R CMD check.

New-Conversation Handoff Block

We are starting a new flagship, CRAN-grade R package in this repository: `rcapsule` — an open-source reproducibility capsule compiler and containerizer (Docker + Apptainer) for R projects, Quarto manuscripts, and Shiny apps.

Project mission: Go beyond `renv` by freezing the entire R + OS + scientific toolchain stack and cryptographically verifying computational reproducibility:
1. Full-stack project scanner inspecting R/Quarto/Shiny files, `DESCRIPTION`, and `renv.lock` to detect R packages, OS system libraries, C++/CmdStan/RTMB/JAGS toolchains, Python/reticulate, and LaTeX.
2. Multi-target container compiler generating cached multi-stage Dockerfiles, multi-service `docker-compose.yml` stacks (including Shiny + async worker templates), and HPC-compatible Apptainer `.def` recipes.
3. Cryptographic provenance manifest (`capsule.json`) recording environment digests, RNG seeds, and SHA-256 hashes of inputs/outputs.
4. Verification auditor that re-runs pipelines in isolated containers (with a deterministic local sandbox/mock runner so 100% of `testthat` tests pass on macOS even when Docker is unavailable, plus guarded live-Docker tests) and outputs a journal-ready reproducibility certificate.

Please start by inspecting this repo, designing the architecture (`ARCHITECTURE.md`) and phased build plan, and then we will build iteratively to full tests, vignettes, and a clean `R CMD check`.
